topic: How does the hierarchical classification framework impact satellite link budget margins when prioritizing QoS-sensitive traffic?
consensus_response: Hierarchical classification frameworks significantly impact satellite link budget margins when prioritizing QoS-sensitive traffic, primarily due to limited bandwidth and increased interference. The design of these frameworks relies on traffic aggregation, which can lead to suboptimal resource allocation. This, in turn, impacts link budget margins and QoS support for sensitive traffic. Advanced techniques like array factor analysis and spacing effects optimization aim to improve link budget calculations, but they may not fully address the root causes of interference. A more balanced approach to traffic aggregation and link margin optimization is needed, particularly for satellite networks with high latency, to ensure QoS requirements are met and network performance is maintained.
